rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: This parent declares no global exhibits, so the baseline surface is the case title, the case summary, the parent stem and the part itself. That summary is substantive: it names a 74-year-old on hospital day 14 who has just completed piperacillin-tazobactam and levofloxacin, takes chronic prednisone and methotrexate and a proton pump inhibitor, and has developed frequent watery foul-smelling stools with fever, leukocytosis, hypokalaemia, mild acute kidney injury, dehydration and abdominal distension; the parent stem repeats the same cue cluster. The stem supplies the loperamide order itself. Suspected C. difficile infection with fever, leucocytosis, distension and recent high-risk antibiotics is exactly the setting in which an antimotility agent risks toxin retention, ileus and toxic megacolon, so withholding it and notifying the provider follows without any stage.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage1 must not be the boundary: its orders exhibit states 'The nurse initiates contact precautions for suspected CDI, holds loperamide, and pages the provider' and lists 'discontinue/hold loperamide' among the orders, which is keyed option A performed and then formalised, in both languages. BASELINE is earliest and non-leaking.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: This parent declares no global exhibits, so the baseline surface is the case title, the case summary, the parent stem and the part itself. That summary is substantive: it names a 74-year-old on hospital day 14 who has just completed piperacillin-tazobactam and levofloxacin, takes chronic prednisone and methotrexate and a proton pump inhibitor, and has developed frequent watery foul-smelling stools with fever, leukocytosis, hypokalaemia, mild acute kidney injury, dehydration and abdominal distension; the parent stem repeats the same cue cluster. The cloze is self-framing - it states that CDI is treated with oral vancomycin and asks why - so it does not depend on seeing the prescription in a stage. All three blanks are pharmacology: CDI is a luminal colonic infection, oral vancomycin is minimally absorbed so it stays in the lumen, and intravenous vancomycin does not reach the colonic lumen in therapeutic concentration.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage1 orders oral vancomycin 125 mg four times daily and stage3 continues it, but no stage explains absorption or site of action, so no stage supplies either blank. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: This parent declares no global exhibits, so the baseline surface is the case title, the case summary, the parent stem and the part itself. That summary is substantive: it names a 74-year-old on hospital day 14 who has just completed piperacillin-tazobactam and levofloxacin, takes chronic prednisone and methotrexate and a proton pump inhibitor, and has developed frequent watery foul-smelling stools with fever, leukocytosis, hypokalaemia, mild acute kidney injury, dehydration and abdominal distension; the parent stem repeats the same cue cluster. Each of the six rows is a self-contained clinical vignette carrying its own data, including the row that quotes both leucocyte counts (21.4 down to 18.6). Separating gradual improvement - falling stool frequency with a softer abdomen, improving vitals and labs, and more formed stool - from the escalation patterns of abruptly stopped diarrhoea with rising distension and absent bowel sounds, new peritoneal signs, and hypotension with tachycardia and rising lactate is complication knowledge about ileus, toxic megacolon, perforation and shock.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage2 must not be the boundary: it explicitly records the absence of 'guarding, rebound tenderness, rigidity, hypotension, altered mental status, or ileus', which enumerates the very escalation findings the matrix asks the learner to recognise. stage3 shows the resolved course. BASELINE is earliest and avoids that enumeration.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: This parent declares no global exhibits, so the baseline surface is the case title, the case summary, the parent stem and the part itself. That summary is substantive: it names a 74-year-old on hospital day 14 who has just completed piperacillin-tazobactam and levofloxacin, takes chronic prednisone and methotrexate and a proton pump inhibitor, and has developed frequent watery foul-smelling stools with fever, leukocytosis, hypokalaemia, mild acute kidney injury, dehydration and abdominal distension; the parent stem repeats the same cue cluster. Keyed step A is to recognise the CDI risk pattern from new watery diarrhoea, fever, leucocytosis, recent antibiotics, immunosuppression and abdominal distension - which is precisely the cue cluster the case summary and parent stem already state. From there the order follows safety logic: begin infection control while CDI is only suspected, hold the unsafe antimotility order, use SBAR to obtain testing and treatment orders, then collect the specimen and administer the ordered therapy with ongoing monitoring.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage1 must not be the boundary: its orders exhibit narrates this sequence as accomplished - precautions initiated, loperamide held, provider paged, testing and therapy ordered, then soap-and-water hygiene, dedicated equipment, intake/output, stool counts and skin protection implemented - which discloses steps B through E in the keyed order, in both languages. BASELINE is earliest and non-leaking.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: This parent declares no global exhibits, so the baseline surface is the case title, the case summary, the parent stem and the part itself. That summary is substantive: it names a 74-year-old on hospital day 14 who has just completed piperacillin-tazobactam and levofloxacin, takes chronic prednisone and methotrexate and a proton pump inhibitor, and has developed frequent watery foul-smelling stools with fever, leukocytosis, hypokalaemia, mild acute kidney injury, dehydration and abdominal distension; the parent stem repeats the same cue cluster. The option set itself establishes that an oral vancomycin course is prescribed, and the keyed statement is CDI knowledge: resolution is judged clinically, a test of cure is not recommended once symptoms resolve because colonisation and residual genetic material persist, and the course must be completed with return precautions for recurrent watery diarrhoea, fever or worsening abdominal pain. The distractors fail on the same knowledge, including the alcohol-rub and the immediate methotrexate restart.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage3 must not be the boundary: its discharge exhibit states 'complete a 10-day oral vancomycin course with 6 days remaining at home' and 'no repeat C. difficile test if symptoms remain resolved', which is keyed option A's content delivered as the plan, in both languages. BASELINE is earliest and the only non-leaking boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem restates the three decisive facts - warfarin 7.5 mg nightly on the home list, an INR of 5.2, and active gingival oozing with new ecchymoses - and both baseline exhibits carry them independently, along with the mechanical mitral valve and its 2.5 to 3.5 target. Holding a high-risk medication whose current objective data show likely harm, then verifying or obtaining the hold order and reporting the INR and bleeding, is medication-safety practice; giving the dose, halving it, or deferring the decision to the wife all fail on that standard.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1_1400 records that the provider ordered warfarin held pending INR results and that holding continues, which is keyed option B's outcome. BASELINE is earliest and answerable.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem restates the naproxen exposure and the baseline admission record documents it independently, together with the warfarin, the mechanical valve and the active bleeding. Each keyed response follows from that: document and escalate the exposure because it changes bleeding-risk assessment, teach NSAID avoidance unless the anticoagulation prescriber approves, explain platelet inhibition and gastrointestinal mucosal injury, and route over-the-counter questions through the anticoagulation clinic. The distractors fail on knowledge - permanently eliminating green vegetables, and dismissing two naproxen doses.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_2_2200 must not be the boundary: its teaching exhibit states 'avoid NSAIDs unless specifically approved by the anticoagulation prescriber', 'call the anticoagulation clinic before starting new medications', and 'keep dietary vitamin K intake consistent rather than eliminating green vegetables', which delivers keyed options B and E verbatim and resolves distractor D. stage_1_1400 records the provider notification of naproxen exposure, which is keyed option A. BASELINE is earliest and non-leaking.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem supplies the vitamin K 2.5 mg oral order, and baseline supplies both premises the sentence needs. The initial assessment exhibit documents minor mucocutaneous bleeding without instability - gingival oozing, ecchymoses, a nosebleed that stopped with pressure, blood pressure 106/64, alert and oriented, no melena or haematemesis - and the admission record documents a mechanical mitral valve with an ongoing 2.5 to 3.5 INR target. That a controlled partial reversal must avoid overcorrection to a subtherapeutic INR with valve thrombosis risk is anticoagulation knowledge.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1_1400 contains the same order the stem restates but gives no rationale, and stage_2_2200 shows the INR falling to 4.6 with no further vitamin K, which would demonstrate the controlled-reversal principle rather than inform it. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem restates the entire 0645 data set - INR 6.8, haemoglobin 9.2, new gross haematuria, positive stool guaiac, heart rate 98, blood pressure 100/60 and lightheadedness - so the deterioration is inside the part. Baseline supplies the discharge haemoglobin of 12.8 and the admission 11.4 that make 9.2 a fall, and the home metoprolol and furosemide that row r4 proposes. Prioritising STAT escalation, circulatory support, access and transfusion preparation, and neurologic surveillance while withholding a beta blocker and a diuretic during evolving hypovolaemia is judgement, not lookup.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_3_0645 is the source of the values the stem restates. stage_3_1200 must not be the boundary: it records vital signs every fifteen minutes, continued neurologic checks and transfusion support, which demonstrates rows r2, r3 and r5 as the correct actions. BASELINE is earliest and non-leaking.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem states the orders - intravenous vitamin K and 4-factor PCC for major bleeding - and every keyed action is high-risk medication administration practice: verify orders, allergies, baseline vitals, access, product availability and second-nurse checks; dilute vitamin K and infuse by pump over the ordered time rather than pushing it; monitor for hypotension, flushing, dyspnoea and chest tightness; give PCC promptly per protocol; and reassess bleeding, urine, neurologic status, haemoglobin and repeat INR. The distractor's proposal to delay PCC until vitamin K has been shown to fail is defeated by the same knowledge, since vitamin K takes hours while PCC replaces factors immediately.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_3_1200 must not be the boundary: its nursing-actions text states that vitamin K was 'infused by pump over 30 minutes while monitoring for flushing, dyspnea, chest tightness, and hypotension', that PCC was 'verified with a second nurse and administered per protocol', and that vital signs were taken every fifteen minutes with strict intake/output and hourly urine assessment - keyed options B, C, D, A and E carried out, in both languages. BASELINE is earliest and non-leaking.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem restates the entire 1200 picture - INR 3.8, haemoglobin 9.8 after transfusion support, improved blood pressure, clearing urine, negative head CT, pending gastroenterology and urology consults. Baseline supplies the two facts that make the keyed handoff correct: a mechanical mitral valve and a 2.5 to 3.5 target, so a falling INR carries thrombosis risk while the bleeding source remains unevaluated. The distractors fail on that same tension - restarting warfarin at nursing discretion, standing down neurologic checks, or relaxing monitoring.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_3_1200 supplies the 1200 status the stem restates and notes that warfarin has not been restarted, which bears on a distractor rather than on the key. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: Each row is a self-describing home-oxygen finding, and the classification is fire- and fall-safety knowledge: smoking near an oxygen source, petroleum-based lubricant at the cannula, and tubing across a walkway are hazards, while using the prescribed flow and keeping the backup battery charged are expected behaviours. Baseline supplies the context that makes them apply - a 69-year-old with COPD, a new order for 2 L/min by nasal cannula, a small apartment shared with a spouse, and cane use. Recorded qualifier: the stem attributes the findings to 'the initial home oxygen referral note', while they actually originate in the stage exhibits; because each row restates its own finding, that mislabel does not affect answerability.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_1_home is the source of most rows but classifies none of them. stage_2_teaching would show two of them being corrected - the spouse asking about a water-based lubricant and both agreeing to move the table so tubing does not cross the doorway - which signals rows r2 and r4 as the concerns. BASELINE is earliest and avoids that.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The cloze asks for 'the priority discharge barrier' and restates nothing, and at baseline no barrier exists: the referral note records only age, COPD, the 2 L/min order, the living situation, cane use and a post-ambulation saturation of 92 percent. The keyed barrier is the client's unsafe intent to self-adjust the flow, and that exists solely in stage_2_teaching, where the client says 'If I feel short of breath, I can turn it up until I feel better.' stage_1_home cannot serve as the boundary because it points the opposite way, quoting the client as saying 'I set the machine to exactly 2 liters like the prescription says.'
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_2_teaching supplies the evidence without the answer: it records the client's statement and the spouse's lubricant question but never names the barrier, never says to use the prescribed flow, and never addresses when to seek help. stage_3_equipment is later and concerns delivery and return demonstration. Recorded qualifier: the stem labels this 'the Stage 1 teaching session' while the teaching session is the second declared stage; R4 forbids inferring the boundary from such a label, and the information dependency places it at stage_2_teaching.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The task is ordering four generic discharge steps, and the sequence follows from the baseline fact that this is a new home-oxygen prescription: verify the prescription, use instructions and equipment ordered; confirm delivery, tubing supply and backup power; obtain a fire-safety and tubing-management return demonstration; then document readiness and communicate remaining barriers.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_3_equipment must not be the boundary: it confirms concentrator delivery, a charged backup battery, and that the client and spouse completed a return demonstration of tubing placement and oxygen-in-use signage - steps B and C shown as already done. BASELINE is earliest and answerable.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: All four options are general home-oxygen safety statements decided by knowledge: keeping oxygen away from flames and posting an oxygen-in-use notice is correct, while sitting near a smoker with the cannula hidden, daily petroleum jelly, and running tubing under throw rugs are fire and fall hazards. Baseline supplies the only case fact needed, a new home-oxygen prescription for a client in a small apartment who uses a cane.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_3_equipment must not be the boundary: it states that the client and spouse completed a return demonstration of tubing placement and 'oxygen-in-use signage', which names the distinguishing element of keyed option B. BASELINE is earliest and non-leaking.

rows.earliestBoundaryEvidence: The stem restates both quantities it needs - a portable cylinder containing 600 L of usable oxygen and a prescribed activity flow of 2 L/min - so the computation 600 divided by 2 equals 300 minutes uses no data outside the part.
rows.laterStageLeakCheck: stage_3_equipment is the source of the cylinder volume, which the stem restates verbatim, so it supplies nothing the calculation needs. BASELINE is the earliest answerable boundary.
